why: Galio shrugs off Orianna's ball poke with his magic shield and bulk, then clears the wave with Winds of War and Colossal Smash to deny her the slow push she wants. Once Orianna steps up to contest the crash, Shield of Durand taunts her in place and Justice Punch plus a jungler turn her lack of mobility into a kill. In pro play that priority lets Galio leave first with Hero's Entrance and decide side-lane fights Orianna can only answer late, which drove a 65% win rate in 20 games.
tips: Crash the wave with Winds of War and Colossal Smash, then move first and arrive at the side lane before Orianna finishes clearing.
Save Shield of Durand for when Orianna walks into taunt range to last-hit; taunt, Justice Punch, then let your jungler finish her.
Hold Hero's Entrance until an ally is already engaged, then land on that fight instead of starting from fog.

why: Orianna matches Viktor's waveclear from longer effective range by parking the ball on the wave, so he cannot walk up for a free Death Ray without eating Command: Attack and Shockwave threat. Her shield absorbs his poke trades and her ball zones the narrow river entrances where Viktor wants to place Gravity Field. Pro teams used that neutral control to reach teamfights even, where a multi-man Shockwave out-values Viktor's storm, producing a 64.7% win rate in 17 games.
tips: Keep the ball on the front of the wave so Viktor must step into Command: Attack range to clear with Death Ray.
Save Command: Protect for Viktor's Death Ray trades and return damage while his laser is on cooldown.
Place the ball at river entrances before objectives and hold Shockwave until Viktor or his front line is grouped on it.

why: Viktor answers Syndra by clearing from behind his own wave with Death Ray, staying outside Dark Sphere range while matching her push. Gravity Field placed on himself punishes her walk-up for Scatter the Weak, and his shield from Siphon Power soaks the first burst rotation so Unleashed Power rarely one-shots him. That stability let pro Viktors survive lane and out-scale into teamfight zoning, winning 64.7% of 17 games.
tips: Clear with upgraded Death Ray from max range and never walk past your wave to trade while Syndra holds Scatter the Weak.
Drop Gravity Field at your feet when Syndra steps forward and walk out only after she spends her stun.
Save your shield rotation for her full combo and trade back while Dark Sphere and Scatter the Weak are down.

why: Cassiopeia out-trades Orianna up close with Twin Fang, but Orianna never has to enter that range: she farms and pokes through the wave with the ball and keeps Cassiopeia pinned. Miasma cannot stop ball movement, and Cassiopeia's short range makes her an easy Shockwave target when she tries to chase past the wave. Pro Oriannas kept the lane at arm's length and won the grouped fights, taking 68.8% of 16 games.
tips: Farm with Command: Attack through the wave and only auto-attack Cassiopeia when she steps up for a last hit.
Stay outside Twin Fang range after she lands Noxious Blast; re-engage only when her poison is about to expire.
Hold Shockwave for when Cassiopeia commits forward with Petrifying Gaze and pull her in as she chases.

why: Orianna denies Akali the lane she needs by shoving waves under tower, where Akali's energy and shroud are wasted on farm instead of trades. The ball sits on Akali's likely dash path, Command: Protect shields the first burst, and Shockwave damages her even when she hides in Twilight Shroud. Pro teams used that push to move first and punish Akali's weak early waveclear, winning 56.3% of 16 games.
tips: Shove every wave before level 6 so Akali must spend energy on minions instead of trading onto you.
Keep the ball between you and Akali and shield yourself the moment she lands Shuriken Flip.
Drop Shockwave on your own position when Akali dashes in; it hits her even inside Twilight Shroud.

why: Ryze answers Ahri by hard-shoving with Overload and Spell Flux, removing the minion-free angles she needs for Charm and forcing her to spend mana on the wave. Rune Prison is point-and-click, so Ahri's Spirit Rush dashes do not dodge his root, and he can hold her for a jungler or a burst trade. Pro Ryzes used that push and Realm Warp to match Ahri's roams instead of chasing them, winning 60% of 15 games.
tips: Spread Spell Flux through the wave and clear first, so Ahri has no clear line for Charm.
Hold Rune Prison until Ahri uses a Spirit Rush dash, then root her landing spot for your jungler.
Use Realm Warp to follow Ahri's roam with your wave already pushed instead of walking the river behind her.

why: Ryze matches Anivia's waveclear with Spell Flux bounces and survives her burst combo because Rebirth gives her a second health bar he struggles to finish alone. His point-and-click Rune Prison stops Anivia from kiting freely, and Realm Warp lets his team collapse before she can set up Glacial Storm around an objective. Pro Ryzes played for those grouped arrivals rather than solo kills, winning 57.1% of 14 games.
tips: Bounce Spell Flux off the wave to match Anivia's clear without walking into Flash Frost range.
Save Rune Prison for when Anivia steps up to place her wall and root her before the wall separates you from your team.
Call your jungler before committing to a kill; finish the egg together or do not spend your full rotation.

why: Orianna out-ranges Ryze's short Spell Flux and Overload reach, poking him every time he steps up to spread Flux on the wave. Command: Protect shields his root-and-burst rotation, and Shockwave punishes him for standing inside his own wave to clear. Pro Oriannas kept Ryze under tower and arrived at fights with a health lead, winning 61.5% of 13 games.
tips: Poke Ryze with Command: Attack each time he walks up to spread Spell Flux on the wave.
Shield yourself as Rune Prison lands and trade back while his root is on cooldown.
Keep the ball at the river mouth before objectives so Ryze must walk through it to join a fight.

why: Annie punishes Ryze's short range because every Ryze trade requires walking into Disintegrate and Incinerate range with her stun charged. Summon: Tibbers gives her an area stun that Ryze cannot dodge while channeling Realm Warp, and Tibbers keeps damage on him after the first burst. Pro Annies used the permanent stun threat to zone Ryze off waves he must stand in to clear, winning 63.6% of 11 games.
tips: Keep your stun charged while Ryze clears and zone him off the wave without spending it.
Use Tibbers to stun Ryze the moment he starts Realm Warp near your team.
Let Tibbers keep hitting Ryze after your burst; do not recall him while Ryze is still in range.

why: Twisted Fate does not need to kill Ryze in lane: he clears with Red Card and Wild Cards, then Destiny reveals Ryze's Realm Warp plays and Gate puts a Gold Card where Ryze arrives. Point-and-click Gold Card also stops Ryze from running at him during trades. Pro Twisted Fates matched Ryze's map move with a stronger numbers play, winning 60% of 10 games.
tips: Clear with Red Card on the melee minions and leave before Ryze can spread Spell Flux onto you.
Ult after Ryze starts Realm Warp or leaves lane, and land with Gold Card already locked.
Hold Gold Card when Ryze walks at you; the threat alone keeps him from taking the root trade.

why: Viktor controls Annie from range with Death Ray and Gravity Field, so she must Flash or walk through his zone to land a stun. His Siphon Power shield absorbs her first Disintegrate, and Chaos Storm chases her after she commits Tibbers without a dash to escape. Pro Viktors kept Annie at laser range and farmed into a teamfight lead, winning 77.8% of 9 games.
tips: Poke Annie with Death Ray at max range and never step inside her Flash-Tibbers distance without Gravity Field ready.
Place Gravity Field between you and Annie when she walks forward with stun charged.
Save Chaos Storm until Annie commits Tibbers, then drop it on her retreat path.

why: Ryze roots Yone mid-combo with point-and-click Rune Prison, breaking the Fate Sealed and Mortal Steel chain Yone needs to stay on target. Spell Flux clear also denies Yone free push, and Ryze's sustained Overload damage wins the extended trade once Yone's Soul Unbound timer forces him out. Pro Ryzes held root for the dash rather than poking with it, winning 66.7% of 9 games.
tips: Hold Rune Prison until Yone dashes forward, then root him for a full Overload rotation.
Shove with Spell Flux so Yone must use Mortal Steel on the wave instead of stacking it on you.
Stand away from Yone's Soul Unbound return point so he cannot hit you again as he snaps back.

why: Cassiopeia matches Anivia's post-6 waveclear with sustained Twin Fang damage and does not rely on one burst combo that Rebirth can absorb. Miasma grounds Anivia and blocks the repositioning she wants, while Cassiopeia's damage per second can kill both Anivia and her egg in one extended fight if she lands poison. Pro Cassiopeias played for those long trades rather than short pokes, winning 55.6% of 9 games.
tips: Keep poison on Anivia with Noxious Blast and keep casting Twin Fang; win the long trade, not a short poke.
Place Miasma under Anivia when she channels Glacial Storm so she cannot reposition inside it.
Save enough mana and poison uptime to kill the egg immediately after proccing Rebirth.

why: Ryze survives Viktor's laser poke with sustained waveclear and answers Gravity Field by rooting Viktor and walking out before the stun stacks. Spell Flux clear matches Viktor's push, so Viktor cannot pin him and roam, and Ryze's repeated Overload rotations out-damage Viktor once the first laser is dodged. This older-meta entry won 55.6% across 9 games.
tips: Root Viktor and walk out of Gravity Field immediately; do not trade autos inside it.
Spread Spell Flux through the wave to match Viktor's clear without standing on his Death Ray line.
Dodge the first Death Ray, then take the extended trade while it is on cooldown.

why: Syndra keeps Sylas at Dark Sphere range and answers his dash with Scatter the Weak, knocking him back before Kingslayer sustain turns the trade. Sylas also gets relatively little value from stealing Unleashed Power compared with stronger ultimates, so even a successful steal does not flip the matchup. Pro Syndras held their knockback for the dash instead of fishing with it, winning 62.5% of 8 games.
tips: Save Scatter the Weak until Sylas dashes or lands his chain; knock him back mid-combo, not before it.
Poke with Dark Sphere while moving and never stand still in range of his chain.
Place spheres on Sylas's likely dash landing spot so the knockback also stuns him.

why: Orianna trades evenly with Syndra by shielding her burst and returning damage with the ball parked on Syndra's sphere line. Syndra must stand still to cast, which makes her a reliable Shockwave target, and Orianna's waveclear stops Syndra from getting the free push she uses to roam. Pro Oriannas played the neutral game and punished Syndra's immobility in fights, winning 62.5% of 8 games.
tips: Shield yourself when Syndra picks up a sphere and trade back while Scatter the Weak is down.
Keep the ball beside the wave so Syndra must walk into it to last-hit.
Hold Shockwave until Syndra commits to casting on your front line in a grouped fight.

why: Cassiopeia's sustained Twin Fang damage cuts through Galio's tank stats better than burst mages do, and Miasma grounds him so he cannot Justice Punch out of poison range. Galio's taunt requires standing next to her, exactly where Petrifying Gaze and continuous poison punish him most. This older-meta answer won 62.5% of 8 games by winning extended trades Galio wants to shorten.
tips: Keep poison rolling on Galio and kite backward while casting Twin Fang; never let the trade become short.
Drop Miasma under Galio when he starts Shield of Durand so he cannot dash out after the taunt.
Save Petrifying Gaze for when Galio commits forward with taunt, facing him as he arrives.

why: Galio's magic shield and taunt give him a reliable way to sit in front of a burst mage and stop a dash-in combo with Shield of Durand, then answer with Justice Punch and Winds of War waveclear. Hero's Entrance also lets him match early roams instead of conceding side lanes. This older-meta entry won 71.4% of 7 games on a small sample, so the read is less certain than the larger samples here.
tips: Use Shield of Durand as soon as the enemy mid commits onto you or your carry, then follow with Justice Punch.
Clear the wave with Winds of War and Colossal Smash and move first toward the nearest side lane.
Land Hero's Entrance on an ally already in the fight rather than starting a fight from maximum range.

why: Viktor zones Ryze off the wave with Death Ray and Gravity Field, forcing Ryze to choose between farming from range with Spell Flux or walking into laser damage to spread it. His shield soaks Rune Prison burst, and Chaos Storm follows Ryze even when he tries to Realm Warp out of a bad fight. Pro Viktors kept Ryze pinned and scaled into stronger teamfight zoning, winning 57.1% of 7 games.
tips: Laser the wave and Ryze together whenever he steps up to spread Spell Flux.
Place Gravity Field on the wave Ryze wants to clear so he must back off or take the stun.
Hold Chaos Storm until Ryze commits to a fight or starts Realm Warp in place.

why: Akali bypasses Annie's stun threat by threatening from Twilight Shroud and dashing with Shuriken Flip and Perfect Execution before Annie can lock a full rotation. Annie's burst is front-loaded, so if the first rotation does not kill Akali, Akali wins the extended fight with repeated Five Point Strikes. This older-meta entry won 57.1% of 7 games, largely on Akali's ability to choose when the all-in starts.
tips: Wait for Annie to spend her stun on the wave or a teammate before dashing in.
Use Twilight Shroud after Annie starts her combo and keep moving inside it, since her area spells still hit.
Mark Annie with Shuriken Flip, dash in for one rotation, then leave before her next stun charges.

why: Cassiopeia is one of Akali's hardest lane answers because Miasma grounds her, removing her dash mobility, and Twin Fang damage keeps flowing once poison is applied even as Akali moves in Twilight Shroud. Petrifying Gaze also punishes Akali for facing her during a dash-in. Pro Cassiopeias held Miasma for the engage and won all 6 recorded games.
tips: Save Miasma until Akali dashes in, then place it under her feet so she cannot dash back out.
Keep poison on Akali before she enters Twilight Shroud and keep casting Twin Fang at her last position.
Face Akali's dash and save Petrifying Gaze for the moment she commits onto you.

why: Akali answers Viktor because Twilight Shroud drops his targeted pressure, while her dashes cross Gravity Field before the stun can stack. Viktor is immobile once Akali lands Shuriken Flip, and Perfect Execution gives her a second dash to follow his Flash. Pro Akalis waited out the field and killed Viktor on the second rotation, winning 66.7% of 6 games.
tips: Dash across Gravity Field quickly or wait beside it; never stand inside it stacking the stun.
Use Twilight Shroud after Viktor commits to you, then re-engage when his Death Ray is down.
Save your second Perfect Execution dash to follow Viktor's Flash instead of spending both dashes at once.

why: Annie answers Aurora with a charged stun Aurora cannot reliably dodge once Annie closes range or lands Tibbers. Aurora wants short poke trades and resets, but Annie's point-and-click Disintegrate guarantees the trade lands, and Tibbers keeps damage on Aurora after she repositions. Pro Annies held stun to deny Aurora's hop-in poke pattern, winning 66.7% of 6 games.
tips: Keep stun charged and walk at Aurora when she hops forward; the stun threat alone stops her poke.
Use Tibbers to stun Aurora as she lands from a hop, then let Tibbers chase her next reposition.
Do not throw Disintegrate into the wave while Aurora can hop in; hold the rotation for her.

why: Ahri matches Aurora's mobility with Spirit Rush and threatens Charm whenever Aurora hops into a predictable landing spot. Aurora's burst needs her to commit forward, and Ahri can dash out, then re-engage with Fox-Fire and Spirit Rush resets while Aurora's mobility is down. Pro Ahris played for Charm on the landing rather than chasing the first hop, winning 66.7% of 6 games.
tips: Hold Charm until Aurora hops, then aim it at her landing spot instead of her starting position.
Dash out of Aurora's burst with Spirit Rush and re-engage only after her hop is spent.
Use Fox-Fire movement speed to stay at Charm range while Aurora tries to line up her burst.

why: Sylas answers Viktor by dashing through Gravity Field, then sustaining through Viktor's burst with Kingslayer while Viktor has no escape. Stealing Chaos Storm also gives Sylas Viktor's teamfight zone on a more mobile body. Pro Sylas players took the all-in after Death Ray missed and won 66.7% of 6 games.
tips: Dash in only after Viktor spends Death Ray on the wave, then stick with Kingslayer sustain.
Use your chain to pull yourself across Gravity Field instead of walking through it.
Steal Chaos Storm before objectives and drop it on Viktor's back line as you dive.

why: Cassiopeia out-damages Viktor in extended trades because Twin Fang has almost no cooldown once Viktor is poisoned, while Viktor must wait on Death Ray. Miasma grounds him and cuts off his kite path, and her sustained damage does not fall off when his shield expires. This older-meta entry won 66.7% of 6 games on that extended-trade edge.
tips: Land Noxious Blast first and keep Twin Fang casting; win by duration, not by one rotation.
Place Miasma on Viktor's retreat path when he steps up for Death Ray.
Keep moving sideways between Twin Fang casts to dodge Death Ray while staying in poison range.
